words.note: count on = 의지하다. count me in(나도 할래)까지 세트로!

words.ex: Stick the label on the box.
words.note: stick to = 고수하다, stuck in = 갇히다. stick-stuck-stuck!

use: Don't hang up — I'm still here!
mcq: We hung out at the cafe.
We hanged out at the cafe.
We hung at out the cafe.
words.note: hang-hung-hung. hang out(놀다), hang up(전화 끊다)!

use: Nothing beats a hot shower after work.
퇴근 후 뜨거운 샤워만 한 게 없죠.
words.note: beat + 상대(이기다), win + 경기(win the game). beat-beat-beaten!

words.ex: Hurry, otherwise we'll miss the train.
use: Book now; otherwise, prices go up.
The room was small but otherwise fine.
mcq: Leave now, otherwise you'll be late.
Leave now, other way you'll be late.
Otherwise leave now you'll be late.
words.note: otherwise = 안 그러면. 조건을 뒤집는 접속 부사!

words.ex: The design appeals to young buyers.
use: They appealed for help after the flood.
Does this plan appeal to you?
mcq: The idea is appeal to me.
words.note: appeal to + 사람 = ~에게 매력적이다. 광고·마케팅 필수!

words.ex: He didn't respond to my email.
words.exko: 그가 내 이메일에 답을 안 했어요.
use: How did she respond to the news?
mcq: I responded to his message quickly.
words.note: respond to — to 필수! reply to와 같은 패턴.

words.ex: I intend to finish this by Friday.
use: What do you intend to do next?
I didn't intend to hurt you.
mcq: We intend to expand next year.
We intend for expand next year.
words.note: intend to + 동사. plan to보다 의지가 강한 느낌!

words.ex: To be honest, I didn't like it.
mcq: To be honest, I'm not sure.
To be honestly, I'm not sure.
Being honest to, I'm not sure.
I'm honest to be not sure.
words.note: To be honest = 솔직히. h는 묵음(/아니스트/)!

use: He's unlikely to change his mind.
그가 마음을 바꿀 것 같진 않다.
words.note: unlikely to + 동사 / unlikely that절. -ly인데 형용사!

words.ex: She was upset about the results.
mcq: He's upset for about the delay.
The delay is upset about him.
words.note: upset about = ~때문에 속상한. upset-upset-upset 무변화!

mcq: I was nervous about the exam.
I was nervous for the exam about.
I was nervously about the exam.
The exam was nervous about me.
words.note: nervous about = ~ 때문에 긴장한. 발표·면접 감정 표현!

mcq: We have a tight deadline this week.
We have a tightly deadline this week.
We have deadline tight this week.
This week tights a deadline we.
words.note: tight schedule/budget/deadline = 빠듯한. 비즈니스 최빈출 형용사!

use: She has a solid background in finance.
words.note: solid = 단단한 → '믿을 만한, 탄탄한'. 칭찬으로 자주 써요!
ultimately = 이런저런 과정 끝에 결국. finally보다 무게감!

use: Typically, we ship within two days.
mcq: Delivery takes typically three days it.
words.note: typically = usually의 격식 버전. 업무 설명에 딱!

use: We owe our success to the team.
mcq: I owe to him an apology.
words.note: owe + 사람 + 것. I owe you one = 신세 졌어요(회화 필수)!

use: She felt at ease with the new team.
The new road eased traffic downtown.
mcq: A warm bath eases up tension away.
A warm bath makes ease tension.
words.note: ease + 통증/긴장 = 덜어주다. at ease = 편안한. easy의 명사·동사형!

use: 우리는 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
mcq: I don't use that app anymore.
I don't use that app no more anymore.
Anymore I don't use that app not.
words.note: anymore는 부정문과 짝! 긍정문에는 still을 써요.

use: We occasionally eat out on weekends.
Occasionally, the system needs a restart.
mcq: I occasionally check my old emails.
I occasional check my old emails.
I check occasionally sometimes my emails.
words.note: occasionally = sometimes보다 빈도 낮음. occasional(형용사)과 구분!
